provenance: His son's summary, typed in the Claude Code session on 2026-09-13 after that day's telephone call, of his understanding from earlier, undated conversations with Larry. The son's words, verbatim from that message. The "I" in the last clause is Larry's voice carried into his son's summary, not the son's own experience.
text: Larry generally says he volunteered, and liked it there, safer and quieter -  and this is also why I had access to rations outside of the mess hall.
researchNotes: Joins two things Larry said separately: that he volunteered for the mountain (2026-09-13-son-mountain-volunteered.json) and that he had separate rations "because I was gone at The Mountain" (2026-09-13-phone-the-outfit.json, transcribed). On an earlier day, his son reports, Larry described drawing food from a building that was not the mess hall, Whether cash was involved was never asked. His son first noted "not cash", then corrected it the same evening as his own assumption. Open. What the rations were is not stated, and nothing here should be read as more than that. Context, not for putting to him: on the summit he ate what he had and what the strikers shared ("When you are eating sea rations, anything is good", VN-0153). "Sea rations" is his son's spelling of the sound, not a spelling Larry chose (his son, 2026-09-13). That it means C-rations is a reading, so a man rotating up the mountain for a week or ten days at a time would need food drawn in advance rather than a mess hall seat. That is a reading, not his words. Do not offer him a ration type or an allowance to agree with.
